mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the specified horizon more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production slows while employment remains strong, it may indicate inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the specified pattern occurs but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rates during a tightening cycle may negatively impact S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceed 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation as indicated by CPIAUCSL leads to increased costs and potential negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL is high but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts exceed 1300 but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 25% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth coupled with high federal funds rates may indicate inflation concerns, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the specified pattern occurs but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High real consumer spending in a late-cycle expansion may not prevent an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS exceeds 700000 but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.
